AI-first ARR more than tripled past $500M, meaning Adobe is currently monetising the technology the de-rating says will kill it, and a $25B repurchase authorisation retires shares into the discount.
recommendations.key_risk: The bear case is not that Adobe misses a quarter, it is that generative image and video models make per-seat Creative Cloud licensing obsolete over five years, in which case earnings stop compounding and a 10x multiple turns out to have been correct rather than cheap. Concrete invalidation: Digital Media net-new ARR falls year-over-year for two consecutive quarters, or Creative Cloud subscription revenue growth drops below 5%. That is the seat erosion the thesis denies, showing up in the numbers rather than in the multiple. Added by the red team, because it is absent above: the earnings print is not the only dated event inside the accumulation window. Oracle reports the same afternoon (2026-09-10) with an ~11% move priced, and a bad enterprise-software tape that evening moves ADBE independently of Adobe's own numbers — the tranches can fill on someone else's guide.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that cheap software has stayed cheap all year and the positioning evidence is genuinely mixed, not supportive: the fetched analyst trend has bullish share falling 3.1 points with revision direction reading deteriorating, and insiders sold $18.9M against $1.9M bought over six months. SECOND RED-TEAM POINT, ON THE RATIO: 2.95:1 is computed off the 228 ideal, which is the middle of three tranches and 11.4% below the market. recommendations.thesis: About 20% of the world's seaborne LNG passed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war, and Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan on 18-19 March took out two liquefaction trains plus a GTL unit — roughly 12.8 Mtpa, about 17% of Qatari capacity — with QatarEnergy force majeure cancellations to Europe and Asia now running into early November. That makes US Gulf liquefaction the marginal global supplier into winter, and Cheniere is the largest US exporter, running Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi with EIA putting full-year US export volumes near 17.0 Bcf/d.
recommendations.key_risk: Cheniere is a tolling business: the great majority of its volumes are sold under fixed-fee long-term SPAs, so a higher JKM/TTF price only reaches earnings through the smaller portfolio and spot cargo book. A Hormuz de-escalation — Iran said an Oman transit agreement was nearing completion — reopens Qatari flows and collapses the international spread before it ever shows in a quarter. Added by the red team: EIA STEO now expects Middle East shut-in output to recover only in early 2027, which is consensus — the shock has been live since March and is six months old, so the asymmetry here is in the extension of the outage, not in its existence.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the stock has already run 48% off its 200-day low and the supply shock has been live since March, so it is priced. Two things argue otherwise: LNG has lagged XLE by 4.9% over the past month while leading it by 5.6% over three, meaning it consolidated through the very week crude spiked, and it sits 8.3% below its 200-day high while VLO, PSX, OKE and TRGP are all within 4.5% of theirs — this is the least extended large-cap energy name on the fetched screen, not the most. RED TEAM, ON CONVICTION: the technical_level and positioning items are both computed from the same fetched price series and the same nasdaq URL, so this is two independent confirmations (price and the Qatari force majeure), not three. data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a final RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:25 ET that explicitly supersedes an earlier one written at 06:22, so `truncated` is false and nothing in this report is reconstructed. Nine candidates were captured; eight are published and one (XLE) was demoted to the watchlist here in synthesis.

WHAT SYNTHESIS CHANGED. XLE was dropped from the recommendations: its recomputed reward-to-risk is 1.84:1 (entry 63.20, target 67.80, stop 60.70) against the 2.0 swing floor. Its stop is not the problem — 2.21 ATR against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor — so the only ways to clear the floor would have been raising the target or walking the stop in, both of which are the failure the floor exists to catch. It is on the watchlist with the level that would make it work. Every other ratio was recomputed from the final entry, target and downside rather than taken from the notes: ADBE 2.95 (against a stated 190 bear case, not a stop), VST 2.70, LNG 2.05, DG 2.05, KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25 2.13. Stop distances were re-checked in ATRs and all clear their asset-class floors: LNG 2.40, VST 2.42, DG 2.18 against a 2.0 stock floor.

RATIOS CLUSTERED NEAR THE FLOOR — SAID OUT LOUD. LNG at 2.05, DG at 2.05 and the Fed contract at 2.13 sit just above the 2.0 line, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Two things argue they are not: each stop is placed below a real level rather than at a convenient distance (LNG 252.00 below both the 50-day and the 30-day low, DG 116.00 below the 30-day low of 117.51), and the ratios are thin because the entries are close to the market, not because the targets are stretched. The one target worth challenging is LNG's 310, which sits above the 200-day range high of 300.89 — it requires a new one-year high, and the red team should ask why.

EVERY NEW IDEA IS A PULLBACK ENTRY. All four (ADBE 228 vs 257.26, VST 145 vs 151.72, LNG 271 vs 276.02, DG 125.50 vs 127.87) sit below the market, so each fills only once the trade first goes against it. config/strategy.md flags exactly this pattern — the first month ran 31 pullback entries against 1 breakout with a 42% fill rate. In each case the level is a named moving average or confluence rather than a reflex discount, but the skew is real and is not hidden.

CONVICTION IS CARRIED CONSERVATIVELY. LNG lists three distinct kinds of evidence and ADBE four, which by the config/strategy.md table would support 4 and 5 respectively; both are published at the score research assigned (3 and 4). The scores are floors on what the evidence holds, not inflations of it.

DATA GAPS, AND WHAT EACH COST. (1) Options-implied moves are unavailable — yahoo-options returns HTTP 401 for every symbol. Where an implied move appears (ORCL ~11%, ADBE ~8.07%) it is quoted from a named third-party preview and attributed, never computed here. (2) Short interest is unavailable — api.nasdaq.com timed out — so there is no days-to-cover or squeeze evidence on any name today. (3) Index quotes failed on all four sources (finnhub needs a CFD subscription, Yahoo 429, stooq 404); SPY/QQQ/IWM are used as proxies and the index levels in market_context come from a news source rather than a fetch, which is why they are written as annotated strings. (4) Robinhood futures availability could not be verified — the support URL in config/universe.md 404s — so NO FUTURES CANDIDATE WAS CAPTURED, even though a commodity supply shock is the regime that most wants one. That is a real cost of the gap, not a stylistic choice. (5) No dedicated small-cap liquidity screen was run; the small caps that were checked (EE, FLNG, NFE, LCII, SVRA) were reached through themes. VIX and DXY were not fetched.

A TOOL DEFECT, DIAGNOSED AND WORKED AROUND. market_data.py events initially returned zero rows for every macro query and three unrelated sports shard tickers for "Fed", which was first written up as an unavailable source and then corrected at 06:23. Two defects: events() has no server-side search — it pulls one page of open markets and substring-filters client-side, and Kalshi's first 200 open markets are overwhelmingly sports — and it reads prices from the legacy integer-cent yes_bid/yes_ask/last_price keys, which Kalshi now serves as null in favour of yes_bid_dollars/yes_ask_dollars decimal strings. Research fetched the Kalshi API directly instead, so every event price in this report is real rather than estimated. The code was not changed — that needs a test in tests/ — but this is a live bug worth fixing.

ONE SOURCE-VERSUS-FETCH CONFLICT. A Yahoo article states DG "finished at USD 133.21, down 1.8 percent" on 2026-09-08, while the finnhub fetch gives DG 127.87 for 2026-09-08 with 133.21 as the prior close. The fetched data is used throughout; the article appears to describe the 09-07 session.

PRICES ARE 2026-09-08 CLOSES, age about 867 minutes at fetch, market session `pre`. At 6am ET that is the freshest honest equity price — a closed market, not stale data. The Kalshi quote is from 06:24 ET this morning.

COMPOSITION, DECLARED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED. Eight recommendations: one long_term (ADBE), six swing, one event contract. Three of the eight are position closes (LULU, NKE, BCC) rather than new risk. Nothing intraday cleared the bar and nothing was manufactured to fill the lane — the only two dated intraday-grade events in range are ORCL and ADBE tomorrow after the close, both priced for 8-11% moves, which is a coin flip rather than an edge. No crypto: BTC 78,986, ETH 2,489, SOL 103.76, all flat and uninvolved in this regime. No futures, for the verification reason above.

CORRELATION.
